theme.title: Mixed / Stock-Picker's Market
theme.summary: Energy (+1.29%) and Consumer Discretionary (+0.79%) led the market today, while Technology (-2.75%) and Industrials (-1.53%) brought up the rear. That split lines up with a rotation out of growth: growth-oriented sectors averaged -1.08% versus -0.04% for defensives and -0.38% for value and cyclicals, suggesting money moved from high-multiple names into steadier, cash-generative businesses. That shows up at the index level too: the blue-chip Dow gained -1.09% while the tech-heavy Nasdaq fell -2.87%, a wide enough gap to matter. Small caps moved roughly in line with the broader market, with the Russell 2000 at -1.65%. The VIX rose 12.84% to 19.42, pointing to a bit more caution creeping in beneath the surface. Gold slipped 2.97% to $3,884.90, crude oil was little changed at $102.95, and bitcoin gained 0.50% — cross-asset moves weren't all pointing the same direction as equities.
